items.title: NBA Europe Likely Aiming For “Soft Launch” Next Fall
items.summary: The NBA’s aim to start a European league next fall could be a “soft launch” at best, considering the league doesn’t have any teams yet, The Athletic’s Joe Vardon reports. The NBA has partnered with FIBA as it looks to establish its own European league, tentatively known as NBA Europe. “Broadly speaking, it is implausible that a serious league could be launched” by October, a member of a potential NBA Europe franchise ownership group told Vardon. NBA commissioner Adam Silver expressed confidence last month that the new league would move forward, even though negotiations with the existing EuroLeague hit a snag. There’s still no clear resolution, according to Vardon, nor are there any formal agreements in place with the soccer conglomerates, private equity chiefs and tech giants needed to form new teams in Europe’s largest markets. The issue developed in the late stages of his return-to-play process. He’s expected to return to on-court activities in six-to-eight weeks. items.title: Grizzlies’ GG Jackson Undergoes Foot Surgery, Out Minimum Of Three Months
items.summary: Nov. 17: Jackson underwent surgery on Tuesday to repair a broken metatarsal in his left foot, according to the team (Twitter link). He will be reevaulated in approximately three months. Nov. 16: Grizzlies forward GG Jackson II will undergo surgery after breaking the fifth metatarsal bone in his left foot, the team announced today (via Twitter). A return timeline won’t be established until the procedure is complete, but if Jackson’s injury history is any indication, he’ll likely miss most of the 2026/27 season. Jackson broke the fifth metatarsal bone in his right foot a little over two years ago and underwent surgery on September 4, 2024. He didn’t make his 2024/25 debut until January 20, 2025 — roughly four-and-a-half months later. If Jackson is out four-and-a-half months this time around, he wouldn’t return to action until late March/early April. The regular season ends on April 11.…

items.title: Hawks’ Asa Newell Undergoes Toe Surgery, Out Four Months
items.summary: Hawks forward Asa Newell, who sustained a left great toe hyperextension earlier this month, was reevaluated on Monday by a specialist, meeting with Dr. Martin O’Malley in New York, according to the team. Newell underwent additional imaging during that reevaluation that confirmed the hyperextension and also revealed a plantar plate tear in the affected toe. The 21-year-old underwent surgery on Tuesday to treat that injury and is expected to miss most of the rest of the season while he recovers. According to the Hawks, Newell will be reevaluated in approximately four months, which means he’s unlikely to return until mid-to-late March at the earliest. The regular season ends on April 11.
